description: Double TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**20 tokens, so gradient accumulation goes from 8 to 16 micro-steps at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64.
Increase Muon cautious weight decay from 0.2 to 0.3.
Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 for more optimizer steps and scale all learning rates linearly by batch_size/2**19 (0.5x).
Lower UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.002 to reduce the lm_head step size.
A linear LR warmdown to zero already exists (ratio 0.5), so I lengthen it by raising WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7. The model then spends more of the fixed 300 s annealing.
Enable a linear LR warmup over the first 5% of the time budget by setting WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.05.
Make the warmdown polynomial (power 1.5) instead of linear, so the LR tapers more smoothly toward zero.

issues: Integrity is fine. The diff only changes the LR multiplier function: the linear warmdown becomes a step schedule (1.0 up to 50% of training, then 0.5 to 75%, 0.2 to 90% and 0.05 after that). It does not touch the val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines, the evaluation call or the summary printing.

No bug makes the result meaningless. The schedule is well defined across the whole progress range [0, 1] and warmup is kept. The only leftover is that WARMDOWN_RATIO and FINAL_LR_FRAC are probably no longer used by this function. If this candidate were kept, that dead config should be removed.
The numbers support rejecting it. The candidate scored 1.1034 against the incumbent's 1.0989, which is 0.0045 bpb worse, so the negative z has the right sign.

I could not recompute z on my own. There is one run on each side and no noise estimate is given. The reported z = -0.600 implies a noise sigma of about 0.0075, which I cannot check. One run each is a weak basis, but this change looks worse and is not borderline, so a replicate is not worth a slot.

description: Replace the linear warmdown with a step LR schedule (1.0 until 50% of the budget, then 0.5, 0.2 and 0.05 at 50%, 75% and 90%).
Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE again to 2**17 (single micro-batch, no accumulation); the existing LR_SCALE rule rescales all learning rates automatically.

issues: Nothing in the diff touches val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines or the evaluation call. It is a one-line hyperparameter change: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE goes from 2**18 to 2**17.
LR_SCALE is computed from TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE, so this edit also halves every learning rate scaled by LR_SCALE. The effect being measured is smaller batch plus linearly scaled LR, not batch size alone.

If the sequence length is 2048, 2**17 = 64 x 2048, so gradient accumulation drops to 1 step. That is consistent, and I see no bug that would make the result meaningless. If the script checks that the batch divides evenly, the check still passes.

The incumbent mean comes from only 1 run, so there is no incumbent variance. The two candidate runs agree closely (sample SD about 0.0004). z = 4.625 implies a noise SD of about 0.0065 (0.0299 / 4.625), so the harness must use an assumed noise level rather than the observed spread. I can't reproduce it exactly without knowing that noise model. The gap itself is 1.0989 - 1.0690 = 0.0299, which is large and points the same way as the accept decision.
Suggestion: an extra incumbent replicate would make the comparison sturdier. This is not grounds for a veto.

description: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE again to 2**17 (single micro-batch, no accumulation); the existing LR_SCALE rule rescales all learning rates automatically.

A linear LR warmdown to zero already exists, so I shorten it by lowering WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3, which keeps the peak LR longer and decays more sharply at the end (the longer warmdown was worse).
Raise ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 80, so model_dim goes from 512 to 640 (5 heads of 128) at depth 8.
Make attention alternate between sparse (half-context window) and dense (full) layers every other layer by changing WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SL".
Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4 to reduce the token embedding step size.

Use a variable batch size: the first 25% of training uses half the micro-batch (sliced to 32 sequences, ~2**16 tokens) for more early optimizer steps, then it switches to the full 2**17-token batch, with no gradient accumulation.

issues: Nothing found that touches the metric or integrity. The diff changes one line: the AdamW betas for the value-embedding parameter group become (0.9, 0.95). It does not touch the evaluation call, the data, the seed lines, the prepare.py import or the summary printing.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The change is a valid hyperparameter edit. One caveat: the diff does not show what adam_betas is set to. If it is already (0.9, 0.95), this edit changes nothing and the run is effectively a replicate of the incumbent.

The numbers agree with the decision. The candidate scored 1.0693 and the incumbent mean is 1.0690, so the candidate is 0.0003 worse (lower is better). The negative z and the provisional reject both fit that.

I can't recompute z exactly because the two incumbent run values and the harness noise estimate are not given. The reported z = -0.043 implies a noise sigma of about 0.007, which is plausible for a noise estimate pooled across runs. Either way the gap is far below the noise level, so the reject decision stands.

description: Give the value-embedding parameters their own Adam group with slower momentum (beta1 0.9 instead of 0.8) while the other Adam groups keep 0.8.
Raise HEAD_DIM from 128 to 256, so the model has 2 heads of 256 instead of 4 of 128 at the same model_dim of 512 and the same parameter count.
Reduce DEPTH from 8 to 6 and widen to model_dim 576 (ASPECT_RATIO 96) with HEAD_DIM 192 (3 heads), keeping the transformer parameter count roughly constant.
Randomly set 0.5% of training targets to the ignore index (-1) each micro-batch so those tokens contribute no gradient.
No change proposed: the 'Wormhole Trick' is not defined in the spec and I don't recognize it as an established optimizer technique.
Lower MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.03 to reduce the Muon step size for matrix parameters.
